summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes, peripheral vascular disease, and bilateral below-knee amputations was admitted for a revision below-the-knee amputation due to a chronic infection of the right stump with exposed bone. She was started on IV vancomycin, ciprofloxacin, and metronidazole upon admission. An insulin drip was initiated to manage hyperglycemia, later transitioned to a sliding scale. She underwent an uncomplicated revision BKA and had a PICC line placed for outpatient antibiotic therapy, which required repositioning confirmed by chest X-ray. A high vancomycin level prompted a temporary hold in dosing. She was discharged home with home health services on oral and IV antibiotics, pain management, and detailed wound care instructions, with follow-up scheduled in 7–14 days.
